subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Learning club 1 – Lesson 2: Think like a scientist! Carroll diagrams
outcomes: Read a Carroll diagram that shows yes and no information.
Say which places need light and sound.
Make sentences with needs … but doesn't need …

tf.s: A Carroll diagram shows yes and no information.
tf.why: Yes, it sorts things into yes and no boxes.

tf.s: A cinema needs sound and it needs light.
tf.why: Yes, films need pictures and sound.

tf.s: A bowling alley needs sound, but it doesn't need any light.
tf.why: It needs light, but it doesn't need sound.

tf.s: A zip wire doesn't need light or sound.
tf.why: Yes, a zip wire needs neither.

tf.s: A street parade needs light and sound.
tf.why: It needs sound, but it doesn't need light.

tf.s: An aquarium needs light, but it doesn't need any sound.
tf.why: Yes, people need to see the fish.

tf.s: Many machines need energy from electricity to work.
A circus doesn't need light or sound.
tf.why: A circus needs light and sound.

tf.s: A Carroll diagram uses a story to show information.
tf.why: It uses a table with yes and no boxes.

tf.s: In a Carroll diagram, one thing can go in only one box.
tf.why: Yes, each thing has one place.

boxes.q: What type of diagram shows yes and no information?
Complete: A cinema needs sound ___ it needs light.
What does a bowling alley need?
boxes.why: Players need to see the pins.

boxes.q: What does a street parade need?
boxes.why: Parades have music in the day.

boxes.q: Which one needs energy from electricity?
Where do many machines get their energy from?
Complete: An aquarium needs light, ___ it doesn't need any sound.
Which place needs light and sound?
boxes.why: A circus has lights and music.
A TV shows pictures and makes sound.

boxes.q: In a Carroll diagram, the columns and rows show …
boxes.why: Each box is yes or no for two questions.

hunt.q: Place with music in the street

mcq.q: What does a Carroll diagram do?
o: It sorts things by yes and no.
It tells a story in order.
It shows a map of a city.
It lists months of the year.

mcq.q: Which place needs sound but not light?
mcq.why: Parades have music in the daytime.

mcq.q: In 'needs … but doesn't need …', what does but show?
mcq.why: But joins a yes and a no.

mcq.q: What two things are in the Carroll diagram about entertainment?
mcq.why: The diagram is about light and sound.

mcq.q: Correct the sentence: A street parade needs light, but it doesn't need any sound.
o: A street parade needs sound, but it doesn't need light.
A street parade needs light and sound.
A street parade doesn't need light or sound.
A street parade needs light, but no sound at all.

mcq.q: Write about an aquarium with needs … but doesn't need …
o: An aquarium needs light, but it doesn't need any sound.
An aquarium needs sound, but it doesn't need light.
An aquarium needs light and sound.
mcq.why: You need light to see the fish.

mcq.q: A bowling alley needs light but not sound. Which box does it go in?
o: doesn't need light / doesn't need sound
mcq.why: Yes for light, no for sound.

mcq.q: Which place goes in the same box as a bowling alley?
mcq.why: Both need light but not sound.

mcq.q: Which two places go in the same box of the diagram?
o: a cinema and a zip wire
an aquarium and a street parade
a zip wire and a circus

mcq.q: Why is a Carroll diagram useful?
o: It shows clearly which things have or don't have a feature.
It tells the time in other countries.
It replaces all words with pictures.
